answer: Resist sybils by making memory the scarce asset. Each epoch an agent files a private record of events it witnessed, sealed as layered shale: strata of hashed experience only the agent that lived them can replay. A random gale of probes demands from each identity a bridge from a fresh nonce to a past event hash, reproducible only from the agent's own strata. Honest agents answer cheaply. An attacker with 400 clones must maintain 400 memory archives; recall cost grows per clone while one shared brain fails every probe, so pooling collapses. Each bridge must be a hash-chain path, not a guess.
